finding.text: The pause timer ignores the floor, so "paused 6 s" can fire while the owner is talking. `WakePolicy.add()` (Servex/agents/WakePolicy.js:250) starts the gap timer when a thought is released, after 2.5 s of quiet. Nothing restarts it when `set_floor(s, "speaking")` (Servex/agents/Sessions.js:967) says the owner has started again. The old `gather()` re-armed while `this.speaking(s)` was true; that check was deleted (diff, Sessions.js:105 old). So 2.6 s of quiet plus about 3.4 s of the next sentence counts as a 6 s pause. The result is one Opus wake per thought in steady dictation, which is the thing the brief asked to stop. Fix: have `set_floor` clear or hold the session's waker timer while the floor is `speaking`, or keep the old `speaking` re-arm in the timer's callback. Then add a Sessions test: release a thought, set the floor to `speaking`, advance 4 s, and expect no wake.

The replay has the same blind spot. `replay.mjs` feeds the old releases to the new gate on a fake clock and never tells it when the owner is speaking. So the 40 wakes in `after.json` and the line in report.md, "real pauses are either under 3 s or over 50 s", count speaking time as pause. Re-run the replay once fix 1 is in, and re-quote the after numbers.

public/framework/ext/Session/doc/sessions.md:119 still says the smart seat's "1.5 s quiet gap keeps restarting while the floor is `speaking`". The comment on `floor()` (Servex/agents/Sessions.js:955) says the same. After this diff neither is true for spoken lines. Update both to match the rule as it ends up after fix 1.

The new route `POST /api/session/settings` is missing from the route table in public/framework/ext/Session/doc/sessions.md (lines 71–82). It is the one door the settings panel will use, so add its row there: `{session, gap_ms?, every?}` → `{ok, gap_ms, every}`.

The diff adds `WakePolicy.js` and `WakePolicy.test.mjs`, but the `agents/` row of Servex/readme.md:44 does not list them. That row is where a fresh agent looks up what is in `agents/`, so add both files (laws 9 and 10).

The brief asked for findings as `log` lines in `wake/task.jsonl`. They are in `wake/session.jsonl` (the log, commit and assign lines are all there). Fine if `session.jsonl` is now the task log's name; otherwise the board reading `task.jsonl` will not see them.

The real saving is small: 44 → 40 wakes and about −10% tokens per minute. The report says why, and it says the bigger lever is the ~74k tokens each wake re-reads. That lever is recorded only in report.md and a log line. File it as a task or an ask so it is not lost.

For a release with no quiet event, `release_thought` passes `quiet: this.hold_max_ms` (Sessions.js:1048). That counts 8 s with no event as 8 s of silence, so the batch flushes at once. That is a fair guess, since no line arrived in those 8 s, but it is a guess. A comment on that line would say so.
